segments.text: AI tools often invent fake imports that
pass syntax checks, but fail at runtime.
By the end, you will have a foolproof
way to catch those before they break
your code. Brings in the sys module so
we can inspect loaded modules and
manipulate the import system safely.
Imports the builtins module to access
the global namespace where __import__
lives. Captures the original __import__
function before we override it.
Otherwise, we'd lose the ability to
actually import anything. Starts
defining our custom import hook that
will vet every import request before
letting it proceed. This is the core
check. It blocks imports unless the
module is already loaded or is a
built-in, preventing fake or
hallucinated modules. If the module
fails the legitimacy check, it throws a
descriptive importerror to flag
potential hallucinations. Only after
passing the check does it hand off to
the original import function. This is
how real imports still work. This is the
magic moment. We swap the built-in
import function with our vetting wrapper
to enforce the security policy globally.
This import succeeds because OS is
already loaded and thus passes our
legitimacy check. This import fails
because fake_module isn't loaded yet and
isn't a built-in, triggering our
hallucination detection. This hook
intercepts imports at runtime and blocks
anything not pre-registered. Now,
comment. What's your trick to catch fake
imports? Subscribe for a new coding
trick every day.
